 Kaohsiung Turns Purple as BTS Opens the Asian Leg of Arirang
 November 20, 2026 by Contributor 
 Courtesy of BIGHIT MUSIC / Trafalgar Releasing 
 Light shows, a BTS shuttle bus and crosswalks that say "ARMY Go": a Taiwanese port city is rolling out the welcome for 26 shows across nine cities. 
 Even the pedestrian crossings in Kaohsiung have picked a side. Some now flash “ARMY Stop” and “ARMY Go,” with purple hearts, as the Taiwanese port city gets ready to open the Asian leg of the BTS Arirang world tour on Thursday.
 The band plays Kaohsiung on Thursday, Saturday and Sunday. That’s the first three of 21 shows across seven Asian cities. Add five dates in Melbourne and Sydney in February and the run comes to 26 shows in nine cities.
 Courtesy of BIGHIT MUSIC / HYBE 
 A city dressed in BTS purple
 Kaohsiung has been working on its welcome for a while. Purple, BTS’s signature color, now washes over the 85 Sky Tower, Love River, Great Harbor Bridge and Kaohsiung Music Center. The Sky Tower got a surprise extra: a light show that projected messages across its facade, including “The City Is Yours ARMY” and “KH Loves ARMY.” (ARMY, for anyone new to the fandom, is the name of BTS’s official fan club.)
 Love River will also host a musical fountain show during the concert period. Around the city, various events, including K-pop random play dance sessions, will give fans somewhere to go when they aren’t in the stadium.
 Getting around is part of the fun, too. A shuttle dubbed “BUS 613” will carry concertgoers, a nod to BTS’s June 13 debut date. The theme runs through the public transportation system, and Kaohsiung International Airport has set up a BTS-themed photo zone, so the pictures can start the moment fans land.
 Front row, 80 countries wide
 Not everyone can get to Taiwan, and the tour is built with that in mind. BTS’s second Kaohsiung concert, on Saturday, will be screened in around 80 countries and regions on approximately 3,300 screens. Depending on the time zone, the screening will be live or delayed. Fans in Korea can catch it at major multiplex theaters.
 The cinema run doesn’t stop there. The third Jakarta concert, on Dec. 29, will be shown on about 2,800 screens across those same countries and regions. That makes two nights from the Asian leg that fans can watch from a theater seat, wherever they live.
 What’s next on the route
 After Kaohsiung, the tour moves on to Bangkok; Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia; Singapore; Jakarta, Indonesia; Hong Kong; and Bulacan in the Philippines. Then comes Australia in February.
 Courtesy of BIGHIT MUSIC / Trafalgar Releasing 
 Singapore is already planning its own party. BTS is scheduled to play four concerts at the National Stadium on Dec. 17, 19, 20 and 22. The city will also run “BTS The City Arirang – Singapore,” a monthlong celebration with events across town from Dec. 1 to 31, including BTS-themed light shows and fan events.
 Arriving with momentum
 BTS released its fifth full-length album, Arirang , in March and started the world tour the following month. Its most recent shows were in Brazil, where it wrapped up on Oct. 31. On Wednesday, the band also won Most Popular International Artist at the 2026 ARIA Awards, the Australian music awards. That’s a timely win with Melbourne and Sydney on the calendar.
 The trophies have been piling up elsewhere, too. BTS swept six awards at the Melon Music Awards. Its track “Swim” is the only song by a Korean band on Apple Music’s “Best Songs of 2026.” And according to Billboard Japan data, BTS is the first non-Japanese artist to pass 10 billion streams in Japan.
 Off stage, there’s quieter news as well: J-Hope has been supporting a Busan dog shelter with food and new kennels, without making a fuss about it.
 For now, the focus is Kaohsiung: a city that has turned its skyline, its buses and its traffic lights purple for a band, and a tour that’s about to show how far that welcome can stretch.
 Via Korea JoongAng Daily
